subproblem.title: Existence of the translated rectifiable varifold (structure fields)
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U any subset of R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U in the sense of the contract structure RectifiableVarifold (M contained in U, M H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, theta > 0 on M, theta a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, theta H^n-integrable on M cap K for every compact K contained in U), and xi in R^(n+l); put tau(x) = x - xi. Then there is a rectifiable n-varifold V' in tau(U) whose carrier is tau(M) and whose multiplicity satisfies V'.mult(y) = theta(y + xi) for every y in R^(n+l).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ), ∃ V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ ((fun x => x - ξ) '' U), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.carrier ∧ ∀ y, V'.mult y = V.mult (y + ξ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1 and 2 of the parent-supplied proof (definition of V' and verification of its structure fields); the needed translation invariance of H^n (the parent's fact (I1)) is restated in step 0. Notation: M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, H^n := muHE[n], tau(x) := x - xi, sigma(x) := x + xi (the inverse of tau).

0. Preliminary facts. (i) tau and sigma are isometric bijections of R^(n+l) (IsometryEquiv.subRight xi, IsometryEquiv.addRight xi) and measurable equivalences (MeasurableEquiv.subRight xi, MeasurableEquiv.addRight xi); in particular sigma is continuous and a measurable embedding. (ii) muHE[n] is preserved by isometric bijections, so sigma is measure preserving from H^n to H^n (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), hence quasi-measure-preserving, and H^n(tau(S)) = H^n(S) for every set S (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, valid without measurability). (iii) For every set S, tau(S) = sigma^{-1}(S): if y = x - xi with x in S then y + xi = x is in S; conversely, if y + xi is in S then y = tau(y + xi) is in tau(S).

1. Definition. Let V' have carrier M' := tau(M) and multiplicity theta'(y) := theta(y + xi). Once the six structure fields are verified in steps 2-7, V' is a rectifiable n-varifold in tau(U), and the two required equalities V'.carrier = tau(M) and V'.mult y = theta(y + xi) (for all y) hold by definition.

2. carrier_subset: M is contained in U, hence tau(M) is contained in tau(U) (monotonicity of images).

3. nullMeasurableSet_carrier: by (iii), tau(M) = sigma^{-1}(M). The set M is H^n-null-measurable and sigma is quasi-measure-preserving from H^n to H^n by (ii), so sigma^{-1}(M) is H^n-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.preimage).

4. countablyRectifiable: by definition of countable n-rectifiability of M there are a set M0 with H^n(M0) = 0 and maps F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) (j in N), each Lipschitz with some constant K_j, such that M is contained in M0 union (union over j of range F_j). Take M0' := tau(M0) and F'_j(z) := F_j(z) - xi. (a) H^n(tau(M0)) = H^n(M0) = 0 by (ii). (b) F'_j is K_j-Lipschitz, because dist(F_j(z) - xi, F_j(w) - xi) = dist(F_j(z), F_j(w)) <= K_j dist(z, w). (c) If y is in tau(M), then y = x - xi with x in M; either x is in M0, and then y is in tau(M0), or x = F_j(z) for some j and z, and then y = F'_j(z) is in range F'_j. Hence tau(M) is contained in M0' union (union over j of range F'_j), so tau(M) is countably n-rectifiable.

5. mult_pos: if y is in tau(M), then y = x - xi with x in M, and theta'(y) = theta(x - xi + xi) = theta(x) > 0 by positivity of theta on M.

6. aemeasurable_mult: theta' = theta o sigma and, by (iii), H^n restricted to tau(M) equals H^n restricted to sigma^{-1}(M). Since sigma is measure preserving for H^n and a measurable embedding, it is measure preserving from H^n restricted to sigma^{-1}(M) to H^n restricted to M (MeasurePreserving.restrict_preimage_emb), in particular quasi-measure-preserving. As theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M, the composition theta o sigma is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to sigma^{-1}(M) (AEMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving).

7. integrableOn_mult: let K be compact with K contained in tau(U). Then sigma(K) is compact (continuous image of a compact set), and sigma(K) is contained in U: if y is in K, then y = x - xi for some x in U and sigma(y) = x is in U. By the corresponding field of V, theta is H^n-integrable on M cap sigma(K). Moreover tau(M) cap K = sigma^{-1}(M) cap sigma^{-1}(sigma(K)) = sigma^{-1}(M cap sigma(K)), using (iii) and sigma^{-1}(sigma(K)) = K (sigma is injective). Because sigma is measure preserving and a measurable embedding, for every set S the function theta o sigma is H^n-integrable on sigma^{-1}(S) if and only if theta is H^n-integrable on S (MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_comp_preimage). Taking S = M cap sigma(K) shows that theta' = theta o sigma is H^n-integrable on tau(M) cap K.

8. Steps 2-7 verify every field of the structure, so V' is a rectifiable n-varifold in tau(U) with V'.carrier = tau(M) and V'.mult y = theta(y + xi) for every y, which is the assertion.
proof_key_steps: define V' with carrier tau(M) and multiplicity y -> theta(y + xi); both required equalities hold by definition
tau(S) = sigma^{-1}(S) for sigma(x) = x + xi, and tau, sigma are H^n-measure-preserving isometric measurable equivalences
null-measurability and a.e.-measurability of the new fields by pulling back along the measure-preserving embedding sigma
countable rectifiability: translate the null set and compose each Lipschitz parametrization with tau (same constant)
positivity, and integrability on tau(M) cap K via the compact set sigma(K) contained in U and MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_comp_preimage

audit.reason: The prose includes all structure hypotheses and matches the exact Lean proposition. The proof verifies all six obligations: carrier inclusion, null measurability, countable rectifiability, positivity, a.e. measurability and compact-set integrability. Restriction transport applies to arbitrary sets, so no openness or extra measurability assumption is missing. Both asserted field equalities hold by construction.

subproblem.title: Generalized mean curvature transfers to the translated varifold
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U any subset of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U, xi in R^(n+l), tau(x) = x - xi, and V' a rectifiable n-varifold in tau(U) such that mu_V' = tau_# mu_V (V'.weight = Measure.map tau V.weight) and V'.tangentProj y = V.tangentProj (y + xi) for every y. If V has generalized mean curvature H in U (H locally mu_V-integrable on U and integral of div_M X dmu_V = - integral of <X, H> dmu_V for every C^1 compactly supported X with tsupport X contained in U), then V' has generalized mean curvature y -> H(y + xi) in tau(U).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ) (V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ ((fun x => x - ξ) '' U)), V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - ξ) → (∀ y, V'.tangentProj y = V.tangentProj (y + ξ)) → ∀ H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ, V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → V'.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun y => H (y + ξ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: second half of Step 5 and Step 6 of the parent-supplied proof. Notation: mu := V.weight, H'(y) := H(y + xi). The map tau is a homeomorphism (Homeomorph.subRight xi), in particular a topological embedding, and a measurable embedding (MeasurableEquiv.subRight xi); it is injective. By hypothesis V'.weight = mu.map tau, and V has generalized mean curvature H in U, i.e. (A) H is locally mu-integrable on U and (B) integral of V.divM X dmu = - integral of <X, H> dmu for every C^1 map X with compact support and tsupport X contained in U.

1. Local integrability of H' on tau(U) for V'.weight. Let y be in tau(U), say y = tau(x) with x in U. By (A) there is N in the filter nhdsWithin(x, U) with H integrable on N for mu.
(a) tau(N) belongs to nhdsWithin(y, tau(U)): since tau is an embedding, map tau (nhdsWithin(x, U)) = nhdsWithin(tau x, tau(U)) (Topology.IsEmbedding.map_nhdsWithin_eq), and tau(N) belongs to map tau (nhdsWithin(x, U)) because N is contained in tau^{-1}(tau(N)) (image_mem_map).
(b) H' is integrable on tau(N) for V'.weight: the restriction (mu.map tau) restricted to tau(N) equals (mu restricted to tau^{-1}(tau(N))).map tau (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map), and tau^{-1}(tau(N)) = N by injectivity. By MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff, H' is integrable for (mu restricted to N).map tau if and only if H' o tau is integrable for mu restricted to N; and H' o tau = H because H'(x - xi) = H(x - xi + xi) = H(x). So this is the choice of N.
Thus H' is integrable at the filter nhdsWithin(y, tau(U)) for every y in tau(U), i.e. LocallyIntegrableOn H' (tau(U)) V'.weight.

2. First variation. Let X : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l) be C^1 with compact support and tsupport X contained in tau(U). Put Y(x) := X(x - xi), i.e. Y = X o tau.
(a) Y is C^1, as the composition of X with the affine map x -> x - xi.
(b) Y has compact support, because tau is a homeomorphism (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph).
(c) tsupport Y is contained in U: tsupport(X o tau) = tau^{-1}(tsupport X) for the homeomorphism tau (tsupport_comp_eq_preimage). If tau(x) is in tsupport X, which is contained in tau(U), then tau(x) = tau(u) for some u in U, and injectivity of tau gives x = u in U.
(d) Pointwise divergence identity: for every x, V'.divM X (x - xi) = V.divM Y x. Indeed V'.divM X (x - xi) = trace(DX(x - xi) o V'.tangentProj(x - xi)); by hypothesis V'.tangentProj(x - xi) = V.tangentProj(x - xi + xi) = V.tangentProj x; and DY(x) = DX(x - xi) (fderiv_comp_sub, which needs no differentiability hypothesis). Hence V'.divM X (x - xi) = trace(DY(x) o V.tangentProj x) = V.divM Y x.
(e) Change of variables: for a measurable embedding tau and every integrand g (no measurability needed), integral of g d(mu.map tau) = integral of g(tau x) dmu(x) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). Therefore
integral of V'.divM X dV'.weight = integral of V'.divM X (x - xi) dmu(x) = integral of V.divM Y dmu (by (d)) = - integral of <Y(x), H(x)> dmu(x) (by (B), applicable to Y by (a), (b), (c)) = - integral of <X(x - xi), H'(x - xi)> dmu(x) (since H'(x - xi) = H(x)) = - integral of <X(y), H'(y)> dV'.weight(y) (change of variables again).

3. Steps 1 and 2 are exactly the two conjuncts of V'.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun y => H (y + xi)) in tau(U).
proof_key_steps: tau(N) lies in nhdsWithin(tau x, tau U) whenever N lies in nhdsWithin(x, U), since tau is an embedding
integrability of H(. + xi) on tau(N) for mu.map tau reduces to integrability of H on N via MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff
for X in C^1_c with tsupport in tau(U), Y = X(. - xi) is C^1_c with tsupport in U
V'.divM X (x - xi) = V.divM Y x from the tangentProj hypothesis and fderiv_comp_sub
change variables in both integrals with MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and apply V's first-variation identity to Y

audit.reason: The explicit weight and tangent-projection hypotheses match the prose and suffice independently. The proof transports neighbourhood-filter integrability, verifies every test-field condition, establishes the pointwise divergence identity, and changes variables in both first-variation integrals. No openness assumption or circular reliance is needed. Together with the other children and the support intersection identity, it proves the exact selected parent.

subproblem.title: Support of the image of a measure under a translation
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, mu any measure on the Borel sigma-algebra of R^(n+l) (no finiteness assumption), xi in R^(n+l) and tau(x) = x - xi. Then spt(tau_# mu) = tau(spt mu), where spt nu is the set of points x such that nu(N) > 0 for every neighbourhood N of x (Mathlib Measure.support) and tau_# mu = Measure.map tau mu.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (ξ : Amb n ℓ), (μ.map (fun x => x - ξ)).support = (fun x => x - ξ) '' μ.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent-supplied proof's fact (I2) (used in its Step 4), specialised to the homeomorphism tau and proved here in full. Notation: sigma(x) := x + xi, the inverse of tau.

1. For every set N (measurable or not), (tau_# mu)(N) = mu(tau^{-1}(N)), because tau is the underlying function of the measurable equivalence MeasurableEquiv.subRight xi (MeasurableEquiv.map_apply).

2. By Measure.mem_support_iff_forall, a point y lies in spt nu if and only if 0 < nu(N) for every N in the neighbourhood filter of y. Combined with step 1: y lies in spt(tau_# mu) if and only if 0 < mu(tau^{-1}(N)) for every neighbourhood N of y.

3. Inclusion of spt(tau_# mu) in tau(spt mu). Let y be in spt(tau_# mu). We show that y + xi is in spt mu; since tau(y + xi) = y, this gives y in tau(spt mu). Let N be a neighbourhood of y + xi. The map sigma is continuous and sigma(y) = y + xi, so N' := sigma^{-1}(N) is a neighbourhood of y. By step 2, 0 < mu(tau^{-1}(N')), and tau^{-1}(N') = {x : (x - xi) + xi in N} = N. Hence 0 < mu(N) for every neighbourhood N of y + xi, i.e. y + xi is in spt mu.

4. Inclusion of tau(spt mu) in spt(tau_# mu). Let x be in spt mu and let N be a neighbourhood of tau(x). The map tau is continuous at x, so tau^{-1}(N) is a neighbourhood of x, and therefore 0 < mu(tau^{-1}(N)) = (tau_# mu)(N) by step 1. Since N was arbitrary, tau(x) is in spt(tau_# mu) by step 2.

5. Steps 3 and 4 prove spt(tau_# mu) = tau(spt mu).
proof_key_steps: (tau_# mu)(N) = mu(tau^{-1} N) for every set N because tau is a measurable equivalence
characterize the support by positivity of the measure on all neighbourhoods
if y is in spt(tau_# mu) then y + xi is in spt mu, using the neighbourhood sigma^{-1}(N) of y
if x is in spt mu then tau(x) is in spt(tau_# mu) by continuity of tau

audit.reason: The exact type matches the stated arbitrary-measure result. MeasurableEquiv.map_apply permits evaluation on every neighbourhood set, and continuity of translation and its inverse proves both support inclusions. No finiteness, regularity or varifold hypothesis is silently required.

subproblem.title: Tangent projections of a translated varifold
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U and U' arbitrary subsets of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U with carrier M and multiplicity theta, V' a rectifiable n-varifold in U', xi in R^(n+l) and tau(x) = x - xi. If V'.carrier = tau(M) and V'.mult(y) = theta(y + xi) for every y, then V'.tangentProj y = V.tangentProj (y + xi) for every y in R^(n+l), where tangentProj is the contract's orthogonal projection onto the (classically chosen) weighted approximate tangent space where one exists and 0 elsewhere.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U U' : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U') (ξ : Amb n ℓ), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.carrier → (∀ y, V'.mult y = V.mult (y + ξ)) → ∀ y, V'.tangentProj y = V.tangentProj (y + ξ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: first half of Step 5 of the parent-supplied proof. Notation: M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, H^n := muHE[n], eta_{a,r}(z) := blowUpMap a r z = r^{-1} • (z - a) (scalar multiplication •), and HasW(N, w, a, P) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N w a P, which by definition means: finrank P = n, and for every f in C_c(R^(n+l), R) the function r -> integral over eta_{a,r}(N) of f(z) * w(a + r • z) dH^n(z) tends to w(a) * (integral over P of f dH^n) as r -> 0+. Fix y in R^(n+l).

1. The blow-up sets agree: for every r, eta_{y,r}(V'.carrier) = eta_{y+xi,r}(M). Indeed V'.carrier = tau(M), so eta_{y,r}(tau(M)) is the image of M under eta_{y,r} o tau (Set.image_image), and for every x, eta_{y,r}(tau(x)) = r^{-1} • ((x - xi) - y) = r^{-1} • (x - (y + xi)) = eta_{y+xi,r}(x), by the abelian-group identity (x - xi) - y = x - (y + xi).

2. The weights agree: for every r and z, V'.mult(y + r • z) = theta(y + r • z + xi) = theta((y + xi) + r • z) (add_right_comm), and V'.mult(y) = theta(y + xi).

3. Hence for every linear subspace P: HasW(V'.carrier, V'.mult, y, P) holds if and only if HasW(M, theta, y + xi, P) holds. After unfolding the definition, rewriting the integration domains by step 1 and every value of the multiplicity (inside the integrals and in the limit value) by step 2 turns the left-hand proposition literally into the right-hand one; the dimension condition finrank P = n is the same on both sides.

4. Put A(P) := HasW(V'.carrier, V'.mult, y, P) and B(P) := HasW(M, theta, y + xi, P). By step 3 and function and propositional extensionality, A = B as predicates on subspaces. By definition, with the classical decidability instance, V'.tangentProj y = (if h : exists P, A P then (Classical.choose h).starProjection else 0) and V.tangentProj (y + xi) = (if h : exists P, B P then (Classical.choose h).starProjection else 0). The expression (if h : exists P, C P then (Classical.choose h).starProjection else 0) depends only on the predicate C, so substituting A = B shows the two expressions are equal. Hence V'.tangentProj y = V.tangentProj (y + xi); since y was arbitrary, this holds for every y.
proof_key_steps: blowUpMap y r '' tau(M) = blowUpMap (y + xi) r '' M because (x - xi) - y = x - (y + xi)
V'.mult(y + r • z) = theta((y + xi) + r • z) and V'.mult y = theta(y + xi)
the weighted approximate tangent predicates of V' at y and of V at y + xi coincide for every subspace P
equal predicates give equal dependent if-then-else with Classical.choose, so the tangent projections agree

audit.reason: The proof establishes the required equality at every point, matching the prose and Lean type. Blow-up domains and multiplicity arguments agree exactly, yielding equality of the entire weighted tangent predicates. Substituting that predicate equality into the dependent choice expression is valid, including where tangent spaces are non-unique or absent.

subproblem.title: The weight of a translated varifold is the pushforward of the weight
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U and U' arbitrary subsets of R^(n+l), V a rectifiable n-varifold in U with carrier M and multiplicity theta, V' a rectifiable n-varifold in U', xi in R^(n+l), and tau(x) = x - xi. If V'.carrier = tau(M) and V'.mult(y) = theta(y + xi) for every y, then the weight measures satisfy mu_V' = tau_# mu_V, i.e. V'.weight = Measure.map tau V.weight (where V.weight is H^n restricted to M with density ofReal(theta)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U U' : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U') (ξ : Amb n ℓ), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.carrier → (∀ y, V'.mult y = V.mult (y + ξ)) → V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - ξ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent-supplied proof; the needed translation invariance of H^n and change of variables (the parent's fact (I1)) are restated in steps 1, 2 and 5. Notation: H^n := muHE[n], M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, e := MeasurableEquiv.subRight xi (its underlying function is tau and its inverse is y -> y + xi), mu_V := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity(x -> ofReal(theta(x))), mu_V' := V'.weight = (H^n restricted to V'.carrier).withDensity(y -> ofReal(V'.mult(y))). For a measure nu and a set A, nu|A denotes the restriction.

1. tau is H^n-measure preserving: tau is the isometric bijection IsometryEquiv.subRight xi, and muHE[n] is preserved by isometric bijections (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). Hence Measure.map tau H^n = H^n.

2. (H^n|M).map tau = H^n|tau(M). For a measurable equivalence e, every measure nu and every set s, (nu.map e)|s = (nu|e^{-1}(s)).map e (MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map). Apply this with nu = H^n and s = e.symm^{-1}(M), which equals tau(M) (MeasurableEquiv.image_eq_preimage_symm). Since e^{-1}(e.symm^{-1}(M)) = M, we get (H^n.map tau)|tau(M) = (H^n|M).map tau, and H^n.map tau = H^n by step 1.

3. By Measure.ext it suffices to show that mu_V' and mu_V.map tau agree on every measurable set S. Fix a measurable S; tau^{-1}(S) is measurable because tau is measurable.

4. Right-hand side: (mu_V.map tau)(S) = mu_V(tau^{-1}(S)) (Measure.map_apply, tau measurable, S measurable) = integral over tau^{-1}(S) of ofReal(theta(x)) d(H^n|M)(x) (withDensity_apply, tau^{-1}(S) measurable).

5. Left-hand side: mu_V'(S) = integral over S of ofReal(V'.mult(y)) d(H^n|V'.carrier)(y) (withDensity_apply, S measurable). Since V'.carrier = tau(M), the measure of integration is (H^n|tau(M))|S, which by step 2 and MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map equals ((H^n|M).map tau)|S = ((H^n|M)|tau^{-1}(S)).map tau. The change-of-variables formula for a measurable equivalence, integral of f d(nu.map e) = integral of f(e x) dnu(x), holds for every f >= 0 without any measurability assumption (lintegral_map_equiv). Therefore mu_V'(S) = integral of ofReal(V'.mult(x - xi)) d((H^n|M)|tau^{-1}(S))(x). Finally V'.mult(x - xi) = theta(x - xi + xi) = theta(x), so mu_V'(S) = integral over tau^{-1}(S) of ofReal(theta(x)) d(H^n|M)(x).

6. Steps 4 and 5 give mu_V'(S) = (mu_V.map tau)(S) for every measurable S, hence V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - xi).
proof_key_steps: tau is H^n-measure preserving because it is an isometric bijection
(H^n restricted to M) pushed forward by tau equals H^n restricted to tau(M), via MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map
reduce to measurable S by Measure.ext and evaluate both sides with withDensity_apply
change variables with lintegral_map_equiv (no measurability needed) and use V'.mult(x - xi) = theta(x)

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type have identical hypotheses, including arbitrary U'. The proof correctly transports restricted Hausdorff measure, compares weights on measurable sets using withDensity_apply, and applies lintegral_map_equiv before simplifying the multiplicity. It needs neither a sibling theorem nor an unstated finiteness assumption.
